The final common acid-secretory step

A patient with erosive reflux disease begins omeprazole. Gastric acid output falls even when secretion is stimulated by different upstream mediators. Which molecular target explains inhibition of this final common step in parietal cells?

  1. H+/K+-ATPase
  2. Histamine H2 receptor
  3. Muscarinic M3 receptor
  4. Gastrin CCK-B receptor
  5. Carbonic anhydrase alone
Answer and explanation

H+/K+-ATPase

PPIs inhibit the gastric proton pump, downstream of histamine, acetylcholine and gastrin signaling.

Option explanations

H+/K+-ATPase: PPIs inhibit the gastric proton pump, downstream of histamine, acetylcholine and gastrin signaling.

Histamine H2 receptor: H2 blockade affects one upstream pathway.

Muscarinic M3 receptor: M3 blockade affects cholinergic stimulation.

Gastrin CCK-B receptor: CCK-B blockade affects gastrin signaling.

Carbonic anhydrase alone: Carbonic anhydrase is not the PPI target.
